name: Pleegzorg Nederland: pleegzorg.nl (national foster care platform)
coverage: Netherlands (platform of the foster care providers in the sector body Jeugdzorg Nederland)
notes: Information and signposting. A postcode search shows the providers near you, and you ask one of them for an information pack. The pack includes an invitation to a local information evening. The site lists 33 provider entries and 23 foster care regions (the region list says it is not complete).

name: Nederlandse Vereniging voor Pleeggezinnen (NVP, national association of foster families)
coverage: Netherlands (members' association for foster families)
notes: Represents foster families and runs a helpdesk on legal questions for foster carers (per pleegzorg.nl). It does not approve carers. It is one of the bodies behind pleegzorg.nl. Its older address pleeggezinnen.nl does not allow automated reading (robots.txt).

name: Central government information: Hoe word ik pleegouder? (How do I become a foster carer?)
coverage: Netherlands (national government information page)
notes: Information only. Sets out the conditions and steps and sends readers to pleegzorg.nl for the information pack and a local information evening. A separate checklist page lists what a new foster carer must arrange.

name: Raad voor de Kinderbescherming (Child Protection Board): foster care checks and adoption assessment
coverage: Netherlands (national agency of the Ministry of Justice and Security)
notes: Does not take enquiries from people who want to foster: its page sends them to a local foster care provider. It issues the certificate of no objection (verklaring van geen bezwaar, VGB) that every foster carer needs, and it carries out the family study for intercountry adoption. Its adoption page advises against starting a new intercountry adoption (page dated 13 May 2026).

name: Fiom: Adoptievoorzieningen (adoption information and preparation)
coverage: Netherlands (the body appointed to give the compulsory information and preparation sessions)
notes: The old address adoptie.nl now leads here. Its contact page gives a phone line on three mornings a week and an email address for general questions about adoption. It has taken no new intercountry adoption applications since 21 May 2024 and refers people who still want to apply to the Central Authority. It says no one can currently sign up for adoption of a child born in the Netherlands. Support after adoption has moved to INEA.

name: Ministry of Justice and Security: Central Authority for International Children's Affairs (Centrale autoriteit internationale kinderaangelegenheden, Ca IKA)
coverage: Netherlands (central authority under the Hague Adoption Convention)
notes: Carries out the Hague Adoption Convention for the Netherlands. Fiom refers people who still want to start an intercountry adoption here; the Central Authority first talks with them about the small chance of a completed adoption. Contact details are in the government contact guide. Intercountry adoption is being phased out by the end of 2030.

name: Central government information: Adoptie (adoption)
coverage: Netherlands (national government information page)
notes: Information only. Links to Fiom, the Child Protection Board, adoption and foster care leave and INEA. Leads with the plan to end intercountry adoption over 6 years (news of 9 December 2024).

name: William Schrikker Gezinsvormen (WSGV): foster care
coverage: Netherlands (national provider; pleegzorg.nl lists it in almost every foster care region, including Groningen, Drenthe and Zeeland)
notes: Part of the William Schrikker group, which works with children and parents with a disability. It runs regular online information evenings with an experienced foster carer. People can also ask for a brochure or fill in a registration form, after which its intake team gets in touch. Form fields not read.

name: Pleegzorg Drenthe (joint front door of the Drenthe foster care providers)
coverage: Province of Drenthe (joint site of Yorneo, Leger des Heils and William Schrikker Gezinsvormen)
notes: People ask for an information pack or sign up for an information meeting (dates for December 2026 and January 2027 were listed). After the meeting they register with one of the three providers.

name: Yorneo: foster care (pleegzorg)
coverage: Province of Drenthe
notes: Information meetings run through Pleegzorg Drenthe. After a meeting, people ask for a registration pack with a short form: name, street and number, postcode, town, email and an optional question box.

name: Triade Vitree: foster care
coverage: Flevoland; pleegzorg.nl also lists it for Noord-Veluwe (Gelderland)
notes: Information evenings in Lelystad. The information pack form asks for first name, surname, email, phone, address, postcode, town and questions. A second form books a one-to-one talk with a screening worker, a foster care worker or a foster carer, by preferred day and part of day.

name: Pleegzorg Friesland (joint front door of the Friesland foster care providers)
coverage: Province of Friesland (partnership of Alliade, Jeugdhulp Friesland, Leger des Heils Noordoost and William Schrikker Gezinsvormen)
notes: Listed on pleegzorg.nl. Its own site does not allow automated reading (robots.txt), so its enquiry route was not checked. Alliade and Jeugdhulp Friesland describe it as the place for everything about foster care in Friesland.

name: Jeugdhulp Friesland: becoming a foster carer
coverage: Province of Friesland
notes: People ask for information or sign up for an information meeting first. The registration form asks whether you went to a meeting, then for each adult: gender, names, address, phone, email and date of birth; whether children live at home, with their names and dates of birth; the type of foster care preferred; and how you found the service.

name: Alliade: foster care for young people with a disability
coverage: Province of Friesland
notes: Care organisation in Friesland; one of the four partners in Pleegzorg Friesland. Not in the pleegzorg.nl list. The page links to an information evening sign-up and a registration form; form fields not read.

name: Entrea Lindenhout: ikwilpleegouderworden.nl
coverage: Gelderland, Overijssel and parts of Noordoost-Brabant and Noord-Limburg (per its site)
notes: Information meetings online and in Gelderland towns, and joint meetings with councils. The sign-up form asks for the date, number of people, name, town, phone, email, whether you already have the information pack and how you heard about foster care.

name: Leger des Heils (Salvation Army) Oost: foster care
coverage: Overijssel (Twente) and Gelderland; pleegzorg.nl also lists it for Eemland and Zuidoost-Utrecht
notes: A Christian organisation; its page says anyone can apply, religious or not. After an information meeting people download a registration form (Word file), fill it in and email it. The site also offers an information pack.

name: Pleegzorg Groningen (joint front door of the Groningen foster care providers)
coverage: Province of Groningen (joint site of Elker, Leger des Heils and William Schrikker Gezinsvormen)
notes: Runs the information evenings and sends the information packs for the three providers. After a meeting people register for preparation with one of them.

name: Elker: foster carers
coverage: Province of Groningen
notes: Information evenings and packs run through Pleegzorg Groningen. Elker has its own registration form for people who want to become foster carers; form fields not read.

name: Leger des Heils (Salvation Army) Noordoost: foster care
coverage: Friesland, Groningen, Drenthe and IJsselland (Overijssel)
notes: Same national pages as Leger des Heils Oost, with its own registration form (Word file) sent by email after an information meeting. Takes part in Pleegzorg Groningen, Pleegzorg Drenthe and Pleegzorg Friesland.

name: XONAR: foster care and family homes
coverage: Province of Limburg (its page says its area is all of Limburg)
notes: Small information evenings in Maastricht, Heerlen and online; information pack request online. Its page says there is formally no maximum age for foster carers.

name: Scoor Pleegzorg
coverage: South and Central Limburg
notes: Describes itself as a small foster care organisation. Offers a free information brochure, an introductory talk and information evenings. Form fields not read.

name: Pactum Noord-Brabant en Limburg: foster care
coverage: North Brabant and Limburg; pleegzorg.nl lists it for Midden-Limburg and Noord-Limburg
notes: The page gives a phone line for each area and says you can foster from age 21. No enquiry form found.

name: Vigere: foster care
coverage: West-Brabant Oost (Altena, Breda, Drimmelen, Geertruidenberg and Oosterhout, per pleegzorg.nl)
notes: People ask for an information pack or sign up for an exploratory talk, then register. Form fields not read.

name: Sterk Huis: foster care
coverage: Midden-Brabant; pleegzorg.nl also lists it for Noordoost-Brabant and West-Brabant Oost
notes: The information pack form asks for name, phone, email (required), how to be contacted, paper or digital pack, address, postcode, town and a message. A longer registration form (Aanmeldformulier STAP) asks for each adult's details, including date of birth, job, working hours and religion.

name: Oosterpoort: becoming a foster carer
coverage: Noordoost-Brabant; pleegzorg.nl also lists it for Noord-Limburg
notes: People ask for an information pack or sign up for an information evening. The page asks people from other regions to contact the provider in their own region through pleegzorg.nl. Form fields not read.

name: Combinatie Jeugdzorg: foster care
coverage: Zuidoost-Brabant
notes: The page offers an information pack and information meetings and says it works with about 450 foster families in Zuidoost-Brabant. Its 'I want to become a foster carer' page returned 404 when we checked.

name: Kenter Jeugdhulp: foster care
coverage: North Holland (Kennemerland area; the foster care area is not stated on the pages read)
notes: People sign up and are then invited to an information meeting. The contact form asks who you want to talk to (a foster care worker, a foster carer or a project family), your name, email, phone and the best days and times to reach you.

name: Parlan: becoming a foster carer
coverage: North Holland (Noord-Holland Noord area; the region list on its page was not captured)
notes: The information pack form asks for name, town, email and how you heard about foster care. It then invites people to a personal talk or sends stories about foster care.

name: Levvel: becoming a foster carer
coverage: Amsterdam area; a municipal page seen in search results also lists it for Zaanstreek-Waterland
notes: Information evenings online or at its Amsterdam location, led by a trainer. People can also ask for more information. Form fields not read.

name: Pactum Gelderland en Overijssel: foster care
coverage: Gelderland and Overijssel (locations in Arnhem, Deventer and Harderwijk)
notes: Listed separately from Pactum Noord-Brabant en Limburg on pleegzorg.nl. The shared Pactum page gives a phone line for Gelderland and Overijssel. No enquiry form found.

name: Jarabee: foster care
coverage: Twente area of Overijssel (address in Hengelo; the area is not stated on the pages read)
notes: Its news page announced an information evening on 21 October 2026. The criteria page says you need to be 21, have a spare bedroom and a stable situation. The address on pleegzorg.nl for its foster carer pages returned 404.

name: Trias Jeugdhulp: foster carers
coverage: Zwolle, IJsselland and Twente; pleegzorg.nl also lists it for Midden-IJssel and Oost-Veluwe
notes: The foster carers page we read showed stories but no enquiry route; the forms we found were for professionals referring a child.

name: De Rading: foster care
coverage: Eemland, Foodvalley, Gooi en Vechtstreek, Lekstroom, Midden-Holland, Noord-Veluwe, Utrecht-West and Zuidoost-Utrecht
notes: Regular free information evenings online and on site, always with an experienced foster carer; a personal talk is also possible. Its page says the preparation and registration cost nothing.

name: Timon: foster care
coverage: Several provinces: pleegzorg.nl lists it for Eemland, Foodvalley, Holland Rijnland, Lekstroom, Midden-IJssel and Oost-Veluwe, Noord-Veluwe, Rijnmond, Rivierenland, Utrecht-West, West-Brabant Oost and Zuidoost-Utrecht; it also works in Zeeland
notes: Christian organisation based in Zeist. Its site refused our reader (HTTP 403), so the enquiry route was not checked. A municipal page seen in search results also lists it for Zaanstreek-Waterland in North Holland.

name: Youké: foster care
coverage: Eemland, Foodvalley, Lekstroom, Utrecht-West and Zuidoost-Utrecht (per pleegzorg.nl)
notes: Seven steps: explore, information evening, intake talk, training for prospective foster carers, family assessment, matching and support. People can also ask for an information pack.

name: KOOS Utrecht: becoming a foster carer
coverage: Western part of the city of Utrecht
notes: People ask for the information pack by email or call a named contact. KOOS and Spoor030 run Utregs Plekkie together.

name: Spoor030: becoming a foster carer
coverage: Eastern part of the city of Utrecht
notes: A postcode check sends people in western Utrecht to KOOS. People can register, ask for the brochure or use a contact form. The page says two references are checked. Form fields not read.

name: Utregs Plekkie (joint foster care recruitment for the city of Utrecht)
coverage: City of Utrecht (initiative of KOOS Utrecht and Spoor030)
notes: People contact KOOS or Spoor030 by email or phone to register. The site also has a newsletter sign-up.

name: Juvent: becoming a foster carer
coverage: Province of Zeeland
notes: People ask for the information pack or go to an information session. Its news says Zeeland councils recruit with Juvent, Timon and William Schrikker Gezinsvormen.

name: Enver Pleegzorg
coverage: Rijnmond: Albrandswaard, Barendrecht, Capelle aan den IJssel, Goeree-Overflakkee, Krimpen aan den IJssel, Lansingerland, Maassluis, Nissewaard, Rotterdam, Schiedam, Vlaardingen and Voorne aan Zee (per pleegzorg.nl)
notes: People sign up for an information evening or ask for an information pack. Its service centre is open on weekdays. Form fields not read.

name: iHub pleegzorg en gezinshuizen
coverage: Province of South Holland (per its area page)
notes: Information evenings online and in towns such as Gouda (dates listed into February 2027). People can also ask for information. Form fields not read.

name: Jeugdformaat: wordpleegouder.nl
coverage: Haaglanden: Delft, The Hague, Leidschendam-Voorburg, Midden-Delfland, Pijnacker-Nootdorp, Rijswijk, Wassenaar, Westland and Zoetermeer; its form also lists Voorschoten
notes: Online information evenings and an information pack. The form asks for first name, surname, your municipality (from a list), email, phone and two more fields whose labels our reader could not see. People outside the list are sent to pleegzorg.nl.

name: Cardea: foster care
coverage: Holland Rijnland, Alphen aan den Rijn, Midden-Holland and Haaglanden
notes: The foster care page is written for referrers. It links to a page for current and prospective foster carers, which we did not read.

name: Stichting Mijn Pleegouders: becoming a foster carer
coverage: Based in Utrecht; no area limit stated (guides people to the foster care provider in their own region)
stated_response_time: Within 48 hours by phone, for people who respond to a call for a specific child (binnen 48 uur)
notes: Found through a company database search (Clay), then read on its own website. A foundation that says it is not a foster care provider and does not screen, match or place children. It answers questions, guides people through the process with a regional provider and stays in touch after a placement. The sign-up form asks questions one at a time, including languages, culture and religion; the page says an information pack is sent by email straight away. It also publishes calls for families for specific children.

name: Stichting Wereldkinderen: intercountry adoption
coverage: Netherlands (intercountry adoption from the Philippines, Thailand and South Africa)
notes: Found through a company database search (Clay), then read on its own website. A licensed intercountry adoption body (vergunninghouder), founded in 1971. People can register only once they hold a provisional approval (beginseltoestemming) through the Central Authority. The page says intercountry adoption to the Netherlands will end after 18 December 2030, and that the Central Authority will strongly advise against starting a new procedure.
